key_insight: The PEA organic spacer improves morphology and suppresses lattice defects, slowing degradation of two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites compared with BA under ambient light and thermal stress.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ perovskite nanoflakes.
Assessed environmental light and thermal stability using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Used X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to examine chemical degradation.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: Improved material stability does not establish long-term solar-cell performance; the stability–performance trade-off requires device-level evaluation.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
